record_identity.title: Danfoss refrigeration-control compromises disrupted French supermarkets

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Danfoss refrigeration-control compromises disrupted French supermarkets
incident_identity.date_basis: The bounded Danfoss wave was reported overnight 11–12 October 2026. The later 12–13 October Dixell wave is recorded separately; the combined authority alert does not establish one common operation.

summary: During the night of 11–12 October 2026, refrigeration systems using Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC supervisory controllers were compromised at French supermarkets. Retailers reported altered cooling and defrost operation, overheating of refrigerated storage and the destruction and disposal of perishable food. Multiple retail groups were affected. At Intermarché in La Haye-du-Puits, the store director described a major cleanup and approximately US$112,000 in discarded stock. French cybersecurity authorities issued guidance to restrict remote access and restore affected controllers. The operator and the initial access route were not publicly identified.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: CERT-FR's initial 12 October alert identifies numerous Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC compromises. Reuters and an affected Intermarché director report lost perishable stock and disruption to store operations. The approximate US$112,000 store loss is attributed to that director, not independently audited or extrapolated across stores. National affected-store counts were reported while the investigation was expanding to other controller families and cannot be assigned in full to this Danfoss occurrence. Claroty's earlier research concerns AK-SM 800A vulnerabilities and does not identify the exploit used in the October compromises. The separately reported Dixell events of 12–13 October do not establish a common operator, testing campaign or shared command pathway.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Unauthorised changes to Danfoss-managed refrigeration systems were followed by spoiled food and disrupted supermarket operations. The reported effects span multiple businesses, but the exact control pathway and actor remain unknown. This is a maintainer-authorised cyber-physical context occurrence; AI participation, the purpose of the changes and automated testing have not been established.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A remotely managed operational system can translate unauthorised configuration changes into physical inventory loss and service disruption across stores. This bounded occurrence illustrates infrastructure exposure and operational-control consequences without establishing an AI-origin mechanism.
assessment_boundaries: No occurrence-specific evidence establishes AI assistance, autonomous agents, fuzzing, a maintenance-company test or a specific AI model.
The actor, intention, initial access mechanism and command pathway have not been established.
Reports about rapid changes to Dixell parameters belong to the separately bounded 12–13 October occurrence.
The later Dixell wave is a related investigation, not an established continuation by the same operator.
Earlier AK-SM 800A vulnerability research does not prove exploitation of those weaknesses in older AK-SM and AK-SC controllers.
Published national store counts may include other product families; a precise Danfoss-only count is not established.
The approximately US$112,000 loss is an attributed single-store account, not an audited national loss.
No confirmed physical injury, death or lasting population-wide food deprivation is established.
The maintainer authorised this non-AI-attributed context incident; admission does not establish AI conduct.
Clause-level taxonomy adjudication remains incomplete and no canonical Fidelity Class mapping is asserted.
